# Reference-to-working-entry migration

The 4,472-entry reference snapshot is kept separately. Working entries demonstrate the new four-column format with a sentence and English translation for each applicable form.

| Working entry | Reference handling | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 12 seeded entries linked from vocabulary/INDEX.md | Treat as working demonstrations; check reference membership before any count of unique words | Sample entries prepared |

When upgrading an entry, add a row with the reference file/headword, working file link, retained forms, corrections and verification date. Do not count a promoted entry as a new word. Upgrade further reference entries when the user requests that work.

| [hyle (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/hyle.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0164) | *Hyle* means to make a loud, piercing sound, including crying, screaming, laughter or an alarm. | [høre (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/høre.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0165) | *Høre* has several senses and many fixed combinations, including *høre etter*, *høre fra*, *høre hjemme* and *høre til*. | [høste (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/høste.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0166) | Besides gathering a crop, *høste* means to obtain a result or reward, as in *høste anerkjennelse* and *høste applaus*. | [identifisere (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/identifisere.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0167) | The dictionary also has the reflexive construction *identifisere seg med* (“identify with” or “feel affinity with”). | [informere (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/informere.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0170) | The usual construction is *informere noen om noe*. *Informert* also functions as an adjective, as in *en informert kilde* and *informert samtykke*. | [innlede (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/innlede.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0171) | *Innlede* means to begin or set something in motion, including opening a discussion, event or lecture. | [innrede (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/innrede.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0172) | The dictionary also lists *innreie* as a parallel headword with its own paradigm (*innreier, innreide, innreid*). | [innrømme (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/innrømme.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0173) | *Innrømme* means to acknowledge or admit something; it can also mean to grant/allow someone something, as in *innrømme kunden rabatt*. Dictionary-listed adjectival forms *innrømmede/innrømmete* are less common; *innrømte* is the short form paired with *innrømt*. Examples are original. Checked 2026-11-22. |
| [innse (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/innse.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0174) | *Innse* means to become aware of or realize something. | [instruere (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/instruere.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0175) | The common construction is *instruere noen i noe*. *Instruere om hva en skal gjøre* means to give someone directions about what to do. | [interessere (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/interessere.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0176) | In the common transitive pattern, the thing is the subject and the interested person is the object: *Boka interesserer meg*. | [mye (adjective)](../vocabulary/adjectives/mye.md) | [adjectives](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/adjectives.md#word-0227) | As an adjective/quantifier, *mye* is invariable and used with mass nouns or plural quantity expressions; it does not normally modify a definite singular noun directly, so that cell is inapplicable. *Mye* is also used substantivally and adverbially; those are syntactic uses, not additional adjective forms. Checked 2026-11-22. |

| [klare (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/klare.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0190) | This entry follows the imported meaning “manage,” as in *klare en oppgave*, *klare å gjøre noe* and *klare seg*. Checked 2026-11-22. |

The dictionary lists *kunnet* as a neuter participle; the neuter example shows a restrictive participial use and should be reviewed for naturalness. | [kysse (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/kysse.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0212) | The ordinary sense is to touch someone or something with the lips. Dictionary-listed past forms are *kyssa, kysset, kysste*; participles are *kyssa, kysset, kysst*. Rare definite/plural participial spellings are retained from the source paradigm and may sound unnatural outside set contexts. Examples are authored teaching examples, not dictionary quotations. | [la (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/la.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0213) | The usual construction is *la* + object + infinitive without *å* (*la barna leke*). The source record incorrectly combines the forms of this verb with *lade* ‘load/charge’: *ladde/ladd* and *laende* belong to *lade*, while Ordbøkene gives *lot/latt* and *latende* for this assigned verb. The participial adjective examples are grammatically possible but uncommon; their lexical naturalness merits review. The dictionary gives *latt* in all indefinite genders, with *latte* definite/plural. Passivization is generally avoided in the core allowing/cause senses; the source’s *las* is not confirmed for this dictionary entry. Checked 2026-11-22. |

| [lede (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/lede.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0215) | This entry is the verb *lede*, “guide/direct/lead,” and is distinct from the noun *lede* in the reference snapshot. Other senses include conducting heat/electricity and being ahead in a competition. Examples are original teaching sentences. Checked 2026-11-22. |
| [leke (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/leke.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0216) | *Leke* can mean engage in play, pretend to be something (*leke sjørøver*), or engage superficially with a matter (*leke med tanken*). Adjectival uses are context-specific; examples are authored, and the dictionary’s inflection table supports *lekt* and definite/plural *lekte*. Checked 2026-11-22. |

Although the reference snapshot mechanically supplies participial adjective cells, *lett/lette* are indistinguishable from the adjective meaning “easy/light,” and no natural attributive example clearly shows a participle from this intransitive verb; those cells remain Unverified. The passive examples are impersonal constructions. Checked 2026-11-22. |
| [lette (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/lette.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0219) | *Lette* is polysemous. This entry emphasizes “make lighter/easier,” “relieve,” and “lift,” while also noting the intransitive senses “take off” (aircraft) and “clear” (fog). Past and participle alternatives are *letta* and *lettet*. The dictionary lists *lettede* and *lettete* as definite/plural adjectival participle alternatives; these are retained, though *lettete* is less common and should be reviewed for naturalness. Examples are original. Checked 2026-11-22. |
| [leve (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/leve.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0220) | The verb is normally intransitive, though it can take an object in expressions such as *leve et liv*. Participial adjective examples with *levd* use the phrase “a life that has been lived.” Checked 2026-11-22. |
| [levere (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/levere.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0221) | The verb can mean bring or hand something over, produce a result, or perform well. Examples are original teaching sentences. Checked 2026-11-22. |
| [lide (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/lide.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0222) | Ordbøkene groups *lide* with the alternate infinitive *li* and lays out their paradigms together. The verb is intransitive and commonly occurs with *av* (“suffer from”) or *under* (“suffer under”). The imperative is grammatical but uncommon and literary in ordinary conversation. Adjectival cells remain Unverified rather than forcing rare participles into unnatural sentences. Checked 2026-11-22. |
| [ligge (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/ligge.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0223) | *Ligge* describes a horizontal position, location, and several states or conditions. Ordbøkene also mechanically lists *liegen/ligget* and definite/plural *ligne* as adjectival participle forms; these are not confidently usable as ordinary adjectives and remain Unverified. Do not confuse *ligne* in that table with the separate verb *ligne* “resemble.” *Liggende* is the natural present-participle/adjectival form. | [ligne (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/ligne.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0224) | The main sense “resemble” is usually intransitive with *på* (*ligne på noen/noe*) or reciprocal (*ligne hverandre*). Passive examples and adjectival participles here use that tax-assessment sense, not the ordinary resemblance sense. *Ligna/lignet* are accepted past and participle forms; *lignede/lignete* are definite/plural alternatives. Examples are original teaching sentences. Checked 2026-11-22. |
| [like (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/like.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0225) | This is the verb “like/enjoy,” not the adjective *lik* (“similar/equal”). | [love (verb)](../vocabulary/verbs/love.md) | [verbs](../reference/vocabulary-4472/word-types/verbs.md#word-0226) | This entry covers *love* 3 (“promise/pledge”), not *love* 4 (“praise”). Definite/plural forms are *lova, lovde, lovede, lovete, lovte*. Some alternatives are rare; *lovet* and *lovte* are common Bokmål choices. The present participle *lovende* is also used adjectivally as “promising.” Examples use promise/pledge, not praise. The s-passive example “kundene loves” is formal/stilted; *bli lovet* is the natural passive in most contexts. Checked 2026-11-22. |

Ordbøkene has related but distinct entries: *race* (neuter, a speed competition or contest) and *roadracing* (a specific motorcycle race on a closed asphalt track). Neither establishes the forms or exact sense of this source record. Checked 2026-11-22. |

Futurum rows distinguish intention (skal) from prediction/volition (vil). Conditional rows use ville; skulle is reserved for future viewed from a past context. Checked 2026-11-22. |
